## 🎓 Today's lesson
**What is a "Grey Market Premium" (GMP)?**
In finance, the grey market is an unofficial, unregulated market where shares of a company going through an Initial Public Offering (IPO) are bought and sold before they officially list on the stock exchange. The **Grey Market Premium** represents the extra amount over the official issue price that investors are willing to pay unofficially based on anticipated demand. For example, if an IPO is priced at ₹100 and trades at a ₹30 GMP in the unofficial market, investors expect it to list around ₹130. Because these trades occur outside formal exchange clearinghouses with zero regulatory protection, SEBI recently banned intermediaries from publishing GMP figures to protect retail investors from artificial price manipulation and fraud [[News18]](https://news.google.?oc=5) [[The 420.in]](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiqgFBVV95cUxPUGpmYlVXYjloNTJYSDBzUTFoRFFMczFZMGY2bVdBcVlmeXUwUDNONlUxMjU2QThxWE9mSmM3NGNaWnNDa1dOSl9Oa282WERzYno0dURvR1BkbTUtV19VN2FXZWhxUm1ReTBpQ3ZsUWdTOHZ6WF9xZ3FuTmVXaU1nS1lnYVhKTWVQUEp0WUJZUkdyb3lSZVRkbnBhVjVpeFlDRzEzdFV3RUxYdw?oc=5).
